{{Short description|English phrase}}
{{Other uses}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2023}}
"'''Not even wrong'''" is a phrase used to describe [[pseudoscience]] or bad [[science]]. It describes an argument or explanation that purports to be scientific but uses [[fallacy|faulty reasoning]] or speculative premises, which can be neither affirmed nor denied and thus cannot be discussed rigorously and [[scientific method|scientifically]].

== Origin of the expression ==
The phrase is generally attributed to the theoretical physicist [[Wolfgang Pauli]], who was known for his colorful objections to incorrect or careless thinking.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Shermer M |author-link = Michael Shermer | title = Wronger Than Wrong | journal = [[Scientific American]] | year = 2006 |volume = 295 |issue = 5 | pages =  40|doi = 10.1038/scientificamerican1106-40 |bibcode = 2006SciAm.295e..40S | url = http://www.scientificamerican.com/article.cfm?id=wronger-than-wrong|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110810231612/http://www.scientificamerican.com/article.cfm?id=wronger-than-wrong |archive-date = 10 August 2011 |url-access = subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NNAPngEACAAJ |title=Atom and Archetype: The Pauli/Jung Letters, 1932–1958 |last1=Jung |first1=C. G. |last2=Pauli |first2=Wolfgang |last3=Meier |first3=C. A. |last4=Zabriskie |first4=Beverley |last5=Roscoe |first5=David |date=1 July 2014 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-16147-1 |page=xxxiii |language=en}}</ref> 

[[Rudolf Peierls]] documents an instance in which "a friend showed Pauli the paper of a young physicist which he suspected was not of great value but on which he wanted Pauli's views. Pauli remarked sadly, 'It is not even wrong'."<ref name=peierls>{{cite journal |author=Peierls, R. |title=Wolfgang Ernst Pauli, 1900–1958 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society | volume=5 |page=186 |year=1960 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.1960.0014  |doi-access=free|s2cid=62478251}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Peierls, Rudolf |title=Where Pauli Made His 'Wrong' Remark |journal=Physics Today |volume=45 |issue=12 |year=1992 |page=112 |doi=10.1063/1.2809934 |bibcode=1992PhT....45l.112P}}</ref> This may also be quoted as "That is not only not right; it is not even wrong", or in Pauli's native German, {{lang|de|"Das ist nicht nur nicht richtig; es ist nicht einmal falsch!"}} Peierls remarks that quite a few [[Apocrypha#Metaphorical usage|apocryphal stories]] of this kind have been circulated, and mentions that he listed only the ones personally vouched for by him. He quotes another example when Pauli replied to [[Lev Landau]], "What you said was so confused that one could not tell whether it was nonsense or not."<ref name=peierls />

In this model, a distinction is drawn between things that are simply wrong (e.g., due to an ordinary factual or logical error) and things that are so completely wrong that proving their errors was hopeless.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Thomas |first=Gary |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Education_and_Theory/4Lu-dYhaVPEC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22Not+even+wrong%22&pg=PA15&printsec=frontcover |title=Education and Theory |date=2007-04-16 |publisher=McGraw-Hill Education (UK) |isbn=978-0-335-23027-3 |page=15 |language=en |quote=Pauli had three levels of insult for what he saw as bad science: 'Wrong!', 'Completely wrong!' and 'Not even wrong!' – the last meaning that the work couldn't even be shown to be wrong.}}</ref>

[[Peter Woit]] uses the phrase "not even wrong" to mean "[[unfalsifiable]]".<ref name="Bukerman">{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Burkeman |author-link=Oliver Burkeman |date=19 September 2005 |title=Not even wrong |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/g2/story/0,3604,1573072,00.html}}</ref>
